lines: Phases 1 to 5 complete. Phase 6 in progress. No decision is needed from Brandon now.

Three of round two's five fresh critics have judged, each on a model family its season's builders do not use, at the highest effort, on chain 38's stills beside the approved pictures. Summer: 5 of 10. Fall: 5 of 10. Spring: 6 of 10. None calls its season ready to film. The first two did not have the settled lines of the config, which beat the approved picture where they speak (decision 216, my omission, caught by summer's glass builder), so I read every item of theirs against those lines before it went on and struck two of summer's. Spring's critic had the lines in its order. His eye outranks their scores and mine.

What they named first. Summer: the swirl at the landing hides the house, the tree and the lanterns under an opaque cream mass; the base reads grey brown and in shade where the approved is pale cream lit warm from the right; the table at the lower left carries a soft orange smear. Fall: the shaken leaves are too few, too thin and too rust coloured, so the globe looks half empty; the air at rest is a pale green wash with a flat green band along the bottom of the glass; the fence is a row of upright stakes and the path reads as planks where the approved has a post and rail fence and stone slab steps. Spring: a hard table edge shows behind the globe and the table's petals read as flat sharp cutouts; after the shake the bottom of the globe is a milky pink band where the approved has long bright ribbons of petals over golden light; the glass's highlight is a broad soft sheen where the approved has a narrow crisp rim, and tall tulips and many petals hide the pond and the fence.

I looked at fall's fence, path and left flank at full size beside the approved and the critic is right on all three (two of those pictures are attached). Spring's list came in at 21:30 UTC (2:30 PM MT) and I have not yet looked at its items beside the approved.

Summer's and fall's items are with the nine builders they belong to, ahead of the rest of each list. The close of round two is named: 22:50 UTC (3:50 PM MT). What is not whole then is not pushed and main keeps what it has. Fall's fence and path are a new form that needs a make and a 3840 proof; the builder says how long they take and I decide with the close. Only spring's base has a builder in round two: the base's flat dark front and its mushrooms go to that builder; the rest of spring's list (the table's edge and petals, the glass's highlight, the shake's ribbons, the tulips and the pond) has no builder in this round and goes into the question to Brandon as it stands.

Winter's critic and the critic of the change of season start as places open; all 16 places for agents are in use. Six of the eight strips of the change are in (one is attached); the last two and the sheet across the whole film are due by about 21:50 UTC (2:50 PM MT) by the helpers' own reckoning.

The tenth publish: the page's first pictures are drawn on chain 38 and pushed (agent/p6-first-10, 637ab394). The whole test run and the build of that commit are running here and end about 21:41 UTC (2:41 PM MT). A fresh security review of that commit started at 21:30 UTC. Then come the check of the live page on a helper machine and the publish. Until then the live page is the ninth publish.

A correction to Status 229, which said the first shake's stall is mended on main. One cause is mended: the first shake no longer links a program inside the change. A second remains, stated by the controls builder at 21:13 UTC: on a machine that draws in software a shake can still stall, because the page sends 4,488,000 bytes of particle lists every frame. Its patch sends only the part that is drawn (70 percent fewer bytes at the low level, 40 at medium, none at high), so it makes the stall rarer at low and medium and changes nothing at high or in the film. It goes in after round two's air parts, as its own commit. On a real graphics card: unknown.

After the close: one measuring run of everything together (chain 39), a publish, Preview 07, then the status that gives the live address with stills, says where each season stands and asks whether to move on to the film and the 4K masters. No round three without his word.
Sound credits 7,420 of 10,000 (measured from the ledger, 52 calls), no call since 05:47 UTC on Thursday (10:47 PM MT Wednesday). No film render and no new preview since Preview 06.
